speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long this lesion has been present and if you have noticed any fever or chills?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the history; given your background with Crohn's, diabetes, and a recent steroid use for uveitis, this painful ulcer is concerning for an infection like cutaneous leishmaniasis or a deep fungal infection. Have you noticed the wound edges are raised or undermined, and is there any pus or foul odor coming from the site?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (Lutz-Florian complex) secondary to immunosuppression from Crohn's disease and corticosteroid use. The history of a mosquito/ant bite followed by a painful ulcer with a central necrotic base and undermined borders is classic for this condition, particularly given your compromised immune status. Please confirm if you have traveled to endemic areas (e.g., Middle East, Mediterranean) or been exposed to sandflies.
